Since we assume ⊩ ϕ , it follows that ⊩ ϕ ♭ , and given that every rule in N corresponds to an intuitionistic natural deduction rule, we conclude ⊢ ϕ , as required.

The fl attening technique employed here is strikingly different from standard completeness proofs. However, as the saying goes, ' all theorems were already proved in the Soviet Union '. In particular, this approach bears a strong resemblance to a method developed by Mints [11, 12, 13, 14, 15] from the 1980s for evaluating intuitionistic consequence via resolution systems. Mints' approach systematically transforms proof systems for various logics, including intuitionistic logic, into resolution-based systems while preserving derivational structure. This extends earlier work by Maslov [10] on resolution calculi for classical predicate logic.
